cases.sentence: «Дело в том, что всякий ___ совершается только властью», — говорил он.
cases.translation: "The point is that all progress happens only through power," he said.
cases.explain: Прогресс is the subject of совершается (happens), so it is nominative.

cases.translation: So, then, there is no rent.
cases.explain: Нет (there is no) governs the genitive case (genitive of negation).

cases.sentence: Левин вернулся к первому его ___ и сказал, обращаясь к Свияжскому.
cases.translation: Levin returned to his first point and said, addressing Sviyazhsky.
cases.explain: The preposition к (toward) governs the dative case.

cases.sentence: Возьмите европейскую ___, тем более прогресс в земледельческом быту.
cases.translation: Take European history, especially progress in agricultural life.
cases.explain: История is the direct object of возьмите (take), so it is accusative.

cases.sentence: Если бы сделали то же, да с ___!»
cases.translation: If only they had done the same, but with careful calculation!
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) governs the instrumental case.

cases.sentence: Теперь, в наше время, мы, помещики, при крепостном ___ ввели свое хозяйство с усовершенствованиями.
cases.translation: Now, in our time, we landowners, under serfdom, introduced improvements into our farming.
cases.explain: The preposition при (under/in the time of) governs the prepositional case.

reading.ru: Только если бы не жалко бросить, что заведено.
reading.question: What does the old landowner say would make him abandon his estate?
options: Only if he weren't sorry to give up what he had established
Only if his sons refused to help
Only if the harvest failed completely
Only if the tax collector forced him
reading.correct: Only if he weren't sorry to give up what he had established
reading.explain: He says he would only leave if he weren't sorry to abandon what had been set up (заведено).

reading.ru: «Да вот не бросайте же», — сказал Николай Иванович Свиярский.
reading.question: What does Sviyazhsky urge the landowner to do?
options: Not to give up his estate
reading.correct: Not to give up his estate
reading.explain: Sviyazhsky tells him, "Well, then don't give it up."

reading.ru: Все переделились, ни лошаденки, ни коровенки.
reading.question: What does the landowner say happened to the peasants after the land was divided?
options: They ended up with neither a horse nor a cow
They united into a single farm
reading.correct: They ended up with neither a horse nor a cow
reading.explain: He complains that after the division, the peasants have neither a little horse nor a little cow.

reading.ru: Зато и вы пожалуетесь мировому судье, сказал Свияжский.
reading.question: What alternative does Sviyazhsky suggest to the landowner regarding troublesome workers?
options: That he complain to the justice of the peace
reading.correct: That he complain to the justice of the peace
reading.explain: Sviyazhsky suggests he could also complain to the justice of the peace.

reading.ru: Очевидно, помещик дразнил Свияжского, но Свияжский не только не сердился, но, видимо, забавлялся этим.
reading.question: How did Sviyazhsky react to being teased by the landowner?
options: He was not angry and seemed amused
reading.correct: He was not angry and seemed amused
reading.explain: Sviyazhsky was clearly not angered by the teasing and even seemed amused.

reading.ru: «У меня хозяйство простое», — сказал Михаил Петрович.
reading.question: How does Mikhail Petrovich describe his own farming approach?
reading.correct: Simple
reading.explain: Mikhail Petrovich says, "My farming is simple."

reading.ru: Левин, зная давно эти патриархальные приемы, переглянулся с Свиярским и перебил Михаила Петровича, обращаясь опять к помещику с седыми усами.
reading.question: Why did Levin exchange glances with Sviyazhsky and interrupt Mikhail Petrovich?
options: Because he already knew these old-fashioned, patriarchal methods
Because Mikhail Petrovich was being rude
Because Sviyazhsky signaled him to stop the conversation
reading.correct: Because he already knew these old-fashioned, patriarchal methods
reading.explain: Levin had long known these patriarchal methods, so he turned back to the grey-mustached landowner instead.

reading.ru: Погубила Россию эмансипация!»
reading.question: What dramatic claim does the grey-mustached landowner make about the emancipation of the serfs?
reading.correct: That emancipation ruined Russia
reading.explain: He exclaims, "Emancipation has ruined Russia!"

reading.ru: Помещик, очевидно, говорил свою собственную мысль, что так редко бывает.
reading.question: What did Levin notice was unusual about the way the landowner spoke?
options: He was expressing his own genuine thought, which is rare
reading.correct: He was expressing his own genuine thought, which is rare
reading.explain: The narrator notes the landowner was clearly speaking his own thought, which so rarely happens.

reading.ru: Возьмите реформы Петра, Екатерины, Александра, возьмите европейскую историю, тем более прогресс в земледельческом быту.
reading.question: What examples does the landowner cite to argue that progress requires authority/power?
options: The reforms of Peter, Catherine, and Alexander, and European history
The abolition of slavery in America
reading.correct: The reforms of Peter, Catherine, and Alexander, and European history
reading.explain: He tells them to take the reforms of Peter, Catherine, Alexander, and European history as examples.

reading.ru: «Вот она, рабочая сила, главный элемент хозяйства», — подумал Левин.
reading.question: What did Levin think to himself during the landowner's complaints about workers?
options: That labor is the main element of farming
That the landowner was wrong about everything
That machines were the main element
That land was the main element
reading.correct: That labor is the main element of farming
reading.explain: Levin thought, "There it is—labor, the main element of farming."

reading.ru: Рабочий наш только одно знает — напиться, как свинья пьяный, и испортит все, что вы ему дадите.
reading.question: How does the landowner characterize the Russian worker's behavior?
options: That he only knows how to get drunk like a pig and ruin everything given to him
That he is diligent and careful
reading.correct: That he only knows how to get drunk like a pig and ruin everything given to him
reading.explain: The landowner says the worker knows only how to get drunk like a pig and spoil whatever is given to him.

reading.ru: «То, что уровень хозяйства спускается и что при наших отношениях к рабочим нет возможности вести выгодно рациональное хозяйство, это совершенно справедливо», — сказал он.
reading.question: What point does Levin agree is completely fair regarding the level of farming?
options: That the level of farming is declining and rational farming cannot be run profitably given current relations with workers
That farming should be abandoned entirely
That only machines can save Russian agriculture
That workers should be paid more
reading.correct: That the level of farming is declining and rational farming cannot be run profitably given current relations with workers
reading.explain: Levin says it's completely fair that the level of farming is falling given the current relations to workers.

reading.ru: «Итальянская бухгалтерия», — сказал иронический помещик.
reading.question: What sarcastic remark does the landowner make about Sviyazhsky's accounting methods?
reading.correct: He calls it "Italian bookkeeping"
reading.explain: The ironic landowner mockingly calls it "Italian bookkeeping."

reading.ru: «Я не согласен, что нужно и можно поднять еще выше уровень хозяйства», — сказал Левин.
reading.question: What does Levin say he disagrees with?
options: That it is necessary and possible to raise the level of farming even higher
reading.correct: That it is necessary and possible to raise the level of farming even higher
reading.explain: Levin states he disagrees that it's necessary or possible to raise farming's level even higher.

reading.ru: «Вот это верно», — засмеявшись даже от удовольствия, подтвердил помещик с седыми усами.
reading.question: How did the grey-mustached landowner react to Levin's point about losses?
options: He laughed with pleasure and agreed it was true
reading.correct: He laughed with pleasure and agreed it was true
reading.explain: The grey-mustached landowner laughed with pleasure and confirmed, "That's true."

reading.ru: Хозяйка за чаем только что говорила ему, что они нынче летом приглашали из Москвы немца, знатока бухгалтерии, который за 500 рублей вознаграждения учел их хозяйство и нашел, что оно приносит убытка 3000 с чем-то рублей.
reading.question: What had the hostess told Levin over tea about a German accountant?
options: That they had hired him for 500 rubles and he found the estate was losing over 3000 rubles
That he had made their estate very profitable
That he refused to be paid
That he found no problems at all
reading.correct: That they had hired him for 500 rubles and he found the estate was losing over 3000 rubles
reading.explain: The hostess mentioned they paid a German bookkeeper 500 rubles, and he found the estate was losing over 3000 rubles.

reading.ru: «Ах, рента!» — с ужасом воскликнул Левин.
reading.question: How does Levin react when Sviyazhsky mentions "rent"?
reading.correct: He exclaims with horror
reading.explain: Levin cries out "Ah, rent!" with horror.

reading.ru: Хотите простокваши? Маша, пришли нам сюда простокваши или малины? Обратился он к жене.
reading.question: What does Sviyazhsky do to end the conversation about rent?
options: He offers refreshments (curdled milk or raspberries) and turns to his wife
He challenges Levin to a duel
He calls for the servants to remove Levin
reading.correct: He offers refreshments (curdled milk or raspberries) and turns to his wife
reading.explain: Sviyazhsky changes the subject by offering curdled milk or raspberries and calling to his wife.

reading.ru: Он настаивал на том, что русский мужик есть свинья и любит свинство, и чтобы вывести его из свинства нужна власть, а ее нет.
reading.question: What did the landowner insist about the Russian peasant?
options: That the peasant is a pig who loves piggishness and needs authority to be reformed, which is now lacking
That the peasant is naturally hardworking
That the peasant needs more land
That the peasant is smarter than landowners
reading.correct: That the peasant is a pig who loves piggishness and needs authority to be reformed, which is now lacking
reading.explain: He insists the Russian peasant is a pig who loves piggishness, and only authority (now absent) can fix it.

reading.ru: Крепостное право уничтожено, остается свободный труд, и формы его определены и готовы, и надо брать их.
reading.question: According to Sviyazhsky, what are the options now that serfdom has been abolished?
options: Free labor, whose forms are already defined and ready to be adopted
reading.correct: Free labor, whose forms are already defined and ready to be adopted
reading.explain: Sviyazhsky says serfdom is gone, free labor remains, and its forms are already defined and ready to use.

reading.ru: Этот вопрос занимает теперь лучшие умы в Европе.
reading.question: According to Sviyazhsky, who is currently occupied with the question of organizing labor?
reading.correct: The best minds in Europe
reading.explain: Sviyazhsky says this question now occupies the best minds in Europe.

reading.ru: Помещики встали, и Свияжский, опять остановив Левина в его неприятной привычке заглядывать в то, что сзади приемных комнат его ума, пошел провожать своих гостей.
reading.question: How does the scene end?
options: The landowners stood up, and Sviyazhsky went to see his guests off
A fight broke out between Levin and the landowner
Levin left angrily without saying goodbye
reading.correct: The landowners stood up, and Sviyazhsky went to see his guests off
reading.explain: The landowners got up, and Sviyazhsky went to escort his guests out.
